name: TX-18
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +29 partisan lean
Incumbent Menefee running with large fundraising and outside support
Republican opponent has raised essentially nothing
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 98%
model.rationale: The +29 district lean, Menefee's incumbency and $3.6 million raised against a Republican with no visible fundraising or outside spending all point to a lopsided Democratic win, and Polymarket prices the race at 98% Democratic. No polling or expert ratings exist, so uncertainty stays moderate, but nothing suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling showing an unexpectedly weak Menefee operation or a surge of outside spending against him would be the first sign of trouble.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-18 is a heavily Democratic Houston-area seat with a +29 partisan lean. Incumbent Christian Menefee, first elected in a recent special contest, is running for a full term and has raised about $3.6 million, with more than $7 million in outside support and no recorded opposition spending. Republican Ronald Whitfield has reported no meaningful fundraising or outside backing.

With no public polls or expert ratings available, the race rests on fundamentals: the district's strong lean, Menefee's incumbency and financial advantage, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win near certainty. The forecast is a Safe Democratic hold with a margin near the district's baseline lean.
